The race for faster data processing is pushing infrastructure to its limits, forcing a choice between specialized connectivity and massive storage. You might be deciding between Credo Technology Group (NASDAQ:CRDO) and Western Digital (NASDAQ:WDC) for 2027.

Credo provides high-speed connectivity solutions that enable artificial intelligence data centers to communicate efficiently, while Western Digital is a global leader in both hard disk and flash storage. While they operate in different niches, both are essential players in the scaling of cloud infrastructure. This comparison evaluates which stock offers the best path for long-term growth.

The case for Credo Technology Group

Credo Technology Group specializes in high-speed copper and optical interconnect solutions designed for artificial intelligence infrastructure. The company sells products like Active Electrical Cables and optical components to hyperscale operators and system vendors. It has established key partnerships with Oracle (NYSE:ORCL) and Microsoft (NASDAQ:MSFT) to enhance connectivity for dual-architecture systems.

The demand for faster semiconductor stocks has significantly boosted its financial performance. In the 12 months ended Aug. 1, 2026, revenue reached nearly $1.6 billion, representing a 165.1% increase over the previous period. This expansion led to a net income of roughly $538.3 million and a net margin of about 33.8%.

As of its May 2026 balance sheet, the debt-to-equity ratio is 0.0x, meaning the company carries no debt relative to shareholder equity. Its current ratio is approximately 10.2x, indicating a strong ability to cover short-term debts with current assets. In the fiscal year ended May 2, 2026, free cash flow reached nearly $407.0 million, though stock-based compensation represented roughly 39.3% of operating cash flow, which inflates reported cash generation since SBC is a non-cash expense added back in the cash flow statement.

The case for Western Digital

Western Digital designs and supplies essential data-storage solutions for enterprises and hyperscale cloud providers. Its product portfolio includes both hard disk drives and flash-based storage serving a global market across Asia and the Americas. Customer concentration like this adds a layer of risk, with three individual clients accounting for 16%, 15%, and 13% of total net revenue in its latest annual report.

In the 12 months ended Oct. 2, 2026, revenue reached approximately $14.5 billion, representing a 43% increase compared to the prior year. Net income for this period was nearly $10.0 billion, which indicates a net margin of roughly 69.2%. This performance suggests a robust recovery in cloud storage demand, which now accounts for nearly 89% of its net revenue.

title: NiSource: 3 Key Takeaways for Long-Term Investors

Trading disclosure

On its third-quarter 2026 earnings call, held on Oct. 28, 2026, NiSource (NYSE:NI) raised its long-term financial guidance while expanding its capital investment commitments. The utility is blending standard regulated energy distribution with power contracts for giant technology facilities.

Three things management said stand out.

1. Data Center Expansion Unlocks $1.75 Billion in Customer Savings

NiSource signed a 20-year agreement with Microsoft, marking its fifth data center power contract across three technology giants. The projects run through Genco, the company's power generation segment, and lower electricity bills for retail customers of NIPSCO, its electric utility subsidiary.

With our recently announced Microsoft agreement, Genco now serves 3 of the largest technology companies in the world, and brings our signed agreements to an expected $1.75 billion in savings to existing NIPSCO electric customers.
-- Lloyd Yates, President and Chief Executive Officer

2. Capital Investment Plan Reaches $40 Billion Through 2033

Executive Vice President Shawn Anderson detailed a new seven-year spending forecast that dedicates $32 billion to core regulated utilities and $8 billion to data center generation. Management expects this capital deployment to support compound annual adjusted earnings per share, or net income divided by outstanding stock, growth of 10% to 11%.

Our new 7-year plan totals $40 billion, including $32 billion of base plan investments and approximately $8 billion of Genco investments, to support data center customers.
-- Shawn Anderson, Executive Vice President and Chief Financial Officer

3. Swift Regulatory Recovery Minimizes Capital Drag

Utilities usually wait years to collect revenues on new construction, creating regulatory lag that drags on cash flows. NiSource uses forward-looking rate structures and tracker mechanisms, which are regulatory processes that let utilities recover specific investment costs quickly, to streamline cash generation.

Our new plan improves our cash efficiency by converting over 90% of our investments into initial recovery within 12 months of investment.
-- Shawn Anderson, Executive Vice President and Chief Financial Officer

Looking Ahead

Large technology companies are expanding heavily across Northern Indiana, where available land, water access, and fiber networks give NiSource an operational edge over surrounding power grids. Management is watching regulatory approval schedules and construction milestones to ensure projects open on time.

The shift toward enterprise automation and artificial intelligence has created a fierce battle between two cloud software titans. Investors choosing between Salesforce (NYSE:CRM) and ServiceNow (NYSE:NOW) must decide which platform offers better value.

Salesforce dominates the customer relationship management space, helping businesses track every client interaction. ServiceNow specializes in streamlining back-office workflows, from IT support to HR tasks. Both companies are now racing to integrate generative AI into their ecosystems, making this a pivotal comparison for investors seeking growth in tech stocks.

The case for Salesforce

Salesforce provides cloud-based software that connects sales, marketing, and IT on a single platform to serve over 150,000 companies. It has recently prioritized AI integration through a major partnership with Microsoft (NASDAQ:MSFT) for "Copilotforce," which combines customer context with AI experiences. The company continues expanding its reach through acquisitions such as Braze (NASDAQ:BRZE) to deepen engagement. Salesforce serves businesses of all sizes globally, and no single customer accounts for more than 10% of its total revenue.

In the 12 months ended July 31, 2026, revenue reached approximately $43.9 billion, representing growth of nearly 11.2% over the prior period. The company also generated net income of roughly $9.7 billion, which reflects a net margin of close to 22%. This growth trend has been supported by a steady increase in revenue from $34.9 billion just two years ago. The business focuses on maintaining profitability while scaling its cloud ecosystem and proprietary AI tools.

As of its January 2026 balance sheet, the debt-to-equity ratio is roughly 0.3x, which compares total debt to shareholder equity. The current ratio, a measure of how well a company covers short-term debts with short-term assets, is approximately 0.8x. In the fiscal year ended Jan. 31, 2026, free cash flow was nearly $14.4 billion. Note that stock-based compensation represented roughly 23.4% of operating cash flow, which inflates reported cash generation since SBC is a non-cash expense added back in the cash flow statement.

The case for ServiceNow

ServiceNow offers an AI platform designed to automate enterprise work across departments including IT, human resources, and finance. The company focuses on large enterprise clients, ending recent periods with over 600 customers spending more than $5 million annually. It maintains strategic partnerships with Nvidia (NASDAQ:NVDA) and Accenture (NYSE:ACN) to drive AI-driven workflow integrations for its 8,700 total customers. This strategy targets a growing presence in the public sector and large organizations seeking efficient digital transformation.

title: “Pretty Bizarre”: Microsoft Is Worth More Than Alphabet. Which Makes No Sense
detail:
“Pretty Bizarre”: Microsoft Is Worth More Than Alphabet. Which Makes No Sense
Michael Douglass
Fri, November 20, 2026 at 1:38 PM MST 5 min read
GOOGN
MSFT
META
Explore stocks on Coinbase
Trading disclosure
"Pretty Bizarre": Microsoft Is Worth More Than Alphabet. Which Makes No Sense ©@aukidphumsirichat via Canva, @champpixs from Getty Images via Canva
Key Takeaways

Alphabet hit a 52-week low, leaving it worth $3.34 trillion against Microsoft's $3.70 trillion.

Analysts expect Alphabet to earn about $172 billion over the next 12 months, against about $154 billion for Microsoft.

Amazon and Microsoft trade near 25x forward earnings, while Meta and Alphabet trade near 18x to 19x, even though Google Cloud grew 103% last quarter.

I'd rather own Alphabet, with search growth and 2027 spending plans in its early-February report as the test.

Alphabet (GOOG) hit a 52-week low this week. It's down 20% in a month and 32% below its high, which leaves it worth $3.34 trillion. Microsoft (MSFT:NASDAQ), just 10% off its own high, is worth $3.70 trillion.

One investor in r/ValueInvesting calls that "pretty bizarre":

"At the end of the day, the market cap is supposed to approximate the present value of the future cash flows. I have a hard time seeing Microsoft make more money than Alphabet from now until their eventual bankruptcies."

Which…yeah, agreed.

Microsoft gets the richer multiple

Microsoft trades at 24x the earnings analysts expect over the next 12 months. That's below its five-year average of 29x but well above the 19x it hit in June:

Microsoft (MSFT): forward (NTM) P/E, last 5 years (TIKR)

Alphabet trades at 19x, against a five-year average of 23x. It was at 33x as recently as April:

Alphabet (GOOG): forward (NTM) P/E, last 5 years (TIKR)

So the market has paid up for Microsoft's earnings for years. But Alphabet's earnings have caught up.

Alphabet is expected to earn more

Alphabet's profit more than doubled from 2022 to 2025:

Alphabet (GOOG): net income, $ billions, fiscal 2021-2025 (TIKR)

Its $132 billion of net income in 2025 was about level with the $133.7 billion Microsoft earned in its fiscal year ended June 2026.

From here, Alphabet pulls ahead. Divide each company's market value by its forward multiple, and you get roughly what analysts expect it to earn over the next 12 months: about $172 billion for Alphabet, against about $154 billion for Microsoft.

So investors are paying $360 billion more for the company expected to earn about $18 billion less. Bizarre.

The market is pricing Alphabet like an ad company

The market isn't treating all the big AI spenders alike. Amazon (AMZN:NASDAQ) trades at 25x forward earnings, right next to Microsoft, while Meta Platforms (META:NASDAQ) trades at 18x, right next to Alphabet.

This article first appeared on GuruFocus.

Anthropic (NASDAQ:ANT) closed its first trading day at $97.17 at 4:00 p.m. ET on November 19, up 17.07% from its $83 IPO price on Nasdaq. The ride was wild. The first trade crossed at $111.50 at 11:48 a.m. ET, ran to $114.99 a minute later, then sank to $92.72 by 1:18 p.m. as the wider market slid 2%. Roughly 832 million shares changed hands on day one.

Warning! GuruFocus has detected 3 Warning Signs with NVDA.

Is ANT fairly valued? Test your thesis with our free DCF calculator.

The deal is the largest on record. Anthropic sold 980 million Class A shares for $81.34 billion in gross proceeds after pricing above its $70 to $78 range. A separate $26 billion non-voting placement at $83 brought in Google and Nvidia at about $10 billion each, AMD at $2.5 billion, Broadcom, Micron and Microsoft at about $1 billion each, and TSMC at $500 million. Amazon holds 14.6% and Google 13.4% after the offering, per the final prospectus. Cloud marketplaces generated about 44% of Anthropic's revenue in the first nine months of 2026, according to Fortune, a reminder of how tightly its sales run through partners that are also rivals.

At the close, GuruFocus puts Anthropic's market value at $1.28 trillion. The GuruFocus chart shows a GF Score of just 10/100, which says the listing has almost no public track record of profitability and only middling balance-sheet strength to grade yet, so the score flags data risk more than business quality. Supply is the next test. Up to 315 million insider shares were eligible to sell from day one, and a further 303 million could unlock on December 15. A record pop does not set a floor, and the first quarterly report will decide whether $1.28 trillion is a starting point or a peak.
